title: Compass and Lantern
premise: In the port city of Verrance, on the eve of the Lantern Uprising, Hazel Crane works her late father's typeface bench inside Crane & Sons Print Shop, hiding the fact that she, not her dead brother, is the shop's true master cutter. When census taker Elias Wren discovers a printed pamphlet bearing her secret mark—a compass rose cut into a lantern—she is drawn into the resistance's plan to smuggle proof of the Governor's forged land decrees to a ship bound for the capital. Pursued through three checkpoints by the Governor's men, Hazel must choose between the invisibility she has always guarded and the found family of printers, smugglers, and one reluctant census taker who have come to claim her. The evidence reaches the ship, but only after the print shop burns; Hazel survives, her mark now stamped on a thousand broadsheets, and she finally signs her own name.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring letterpress equipment in coastal mill towns before turning to fiction. His novels explore the quiet rebellions of ordinary tradespeople, and he still prints his own bookplates by hand.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Introduces Crane & Sons Print Shop, Hazel's hidden mastery of the cutting bench, and her ritual of erasing herself from every ledger. Emotional beat: the ache of competence that cannot be claimed.

chapters.title: Census Morning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Elias Wren arrives to count households; Hazel answers as the widow Crane's niece. A dropped pamphlet bearing her secret mark nearly betrays her. Emotional beat: fear coiled under practiced calm.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias notices the pamphlet's mark matches an old typeface commission signed by a dead man. He leaves without reporting it, troubled. Emotional beat: the first crack in a dutiful man's certainty.

chapters.title: The Lantern Uprising Stirs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Rumors of the Governor's forged land decrees reach the print shop via old Marta, the compositor. Hazel refuses involvement. Emotional beat: the temptation to keep her head down versus the itch of injustice.

chapters.title: A Visit After Dark
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias returns privately, not to arrest but to ask who cut the mark. He confesses the census is being used to hunt printers. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared shame.

chapters.title: What the Dead Brother Left
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reveals her brother's death and her stolen identity; Elias promises silence. Marta overhears and instead of betraying her, offers the resistance's contact. Emotional beat: terror turning, unexpectedly, into being seen.

chapters.title: The Cellar Press
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Beneath a chandler's shop, Hazel sees the underground press and meets Tam, a boy runner, and Odile, a smuggler captain. They need her mark to authenticate documents. Emotional beat: belonging offered like a lit match.

chapters.title: Cutting the Compass
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel cuts a new punch—compass inside lantern—for the resistance. Working, she grieves her father and brother properly for the first time. Emotional beat: craft as mourning, craft as defiance.

chapters.title: The Governor's Men
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias is ordered to identify the mark's cutter by week's end. His superior, Inspector Hale, suspects him already. Emotional beat: the noose of complicity tightening.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: the Customs House
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel carries sealed plates hidden in a coffin of 'lead type' through the customs house while Hale watches the queues. Emotional beat: invisibility as armor, worn thin.

chapters.title: Tam's Shortcut
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The boy runner leads Hazel through rope walks and fish markets; his chatter reveals the resistance's fractures—Odile wants payment, Marta wants revolution. Emotional beat: Hazel becoming an older sister despite herself.

chapters.title: The Forged Decree
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias obtains a genuine decree and compares it to the Governor's published forgery; the proof is undeniable. He copies it. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat choosing treason with a steady hand.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Odile agrees to carry the evidence aboard the Morning Tide but demands the compass punch itself as collateral. Hazel refuses; stalemate. Emotional beat: trust bargained for, not given.

chapters.title: Fire in the Type Rack
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A small fire—accident or sabotage—destroys a rack of matrices. Hazel suspects someone inside the cellar press. Emotional beat: paranoia poisoning the first family she's had.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hale traces the coffin shipment to the print shop and schedules a raid. Elias must warn Hazel without exposing himself. Emotional beat: dread measured in hours.

chapters.title: The Widow Crane's Choice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's aunt, the nominal widow, finally learns the truth and shields her before Hale's questions, claiming the mark as her own dead husband's work. Emotional beat: the quiet heroism of the overlooked.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: the Bridge of Chains
chapters.summary: Hazel and Elias's POV, alternating. The pair carries the decree copies across the raised-chain bridge in a census ledger; Elias uses his own authority as cover. Emotional beat: two liars becoming one team.

chapters.title: What Elias Buried
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Backstory: Elias once reported a printer years ago and watched him hang; his obsession with the census was penance. He tells Hazel. Emotional beat: guilt offered up and, haltingly, forgiven.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Mark
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the fire was set by Ferro, the press mechanic, who has been feeding Hale information for his brother's freedom. Emotional beat: a child learning adults break in complicated ways.

chapters.title: Ferrocement
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The resistance debates Ferro's fate. Hazel argues to use him—feed him false plans—rather than punish. Emotional beat: Hazel choosing strategy over vengeance, and surprising herself.

chapters.title: The False Manifest
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The resistance plants a decoy shipment with a forged manifest bearing a corrupted compass mark, letting Ferro 'discover' it. Emotional beat: the hunter turned instrument.

chapters.title: Hale Takes the Bait
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale raids the decoy warehouse, seizes worthless plates, and is humiliated before the Governor. His suspicion shifts fully onto Elias. Emotional beat: a predator's patience curdling into rage.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Census Office
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias is detained and questioned; he burns his copy of the decree in a stove mid-interrogation and walks out for lack of evidence. Emotional beat: terror mastered through sheer procedure.

chapters.title: The Shop Burns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Retaliating, Hale's men burn Crane & Sons. Hazel watches her father's life's work collapse, saved only by Marta dragging her out. Emotional beat: grief and liberation arriving in the same flame.

chapters.title: Nothing Left to Hide
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With the shop gone, Hazel's secret identity is meaningless—she has lost everything she used to hide behind. Marta names her openly as the cutter. Emotional beat: devastation as strange, hard freedom.

chapters.title: Odile's Change of Heart
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile, moved by Hazel's loss and reminded of her own exiled family, waives her price and offers the Morning Tide's hold. Emotional beat: a mercenary choosing a crew over coin.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: the Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Hazel, Elias, and Tam's POV, braided. The real evidence—decrees, matrices, and Elias's testimony—moves in a lantern-oil cart through the harbor gate. Hale waits personally. Emotional beat: the longest hour of their lives.

chapters.title: The Lantern Held High
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hale recognizes Hazel; she bluffs that the cart carries the resistance's real bomb, triggering a panic that scatters his guards. Emotional beat: her invisibility inverted into pure audacity.

chapters.title: Tam Runs the Tide
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam sprints the final quarter-mile to the quay with the sealed case as the tide turns, pursued by a dragoon. Emotional beat: a child carrying a city's truth in his arms.

chapters.title: Elias Stands in the Door
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias blocks Hale on the gangway, formally arresting him in the Governor's name on a technicality of harbor law, buying the loading time. Emotional beat: the rule of law weaponized by a penitent man.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide Sails
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The ship clears the breakwater with the evidence aboard. On the dock, Hale seizes Hazel's wrist as gulls cry. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by capture.

chapters.title: The Uprising Ignites
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. News of the raid and the burned shop sparks the city; printers strike, lanterns fill the streets, the harbor workers refuse to load warships. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into collective power.

chapters.title: Cell by Lantern Light
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Imprisoned, Hazel is offered freedom to name her accomplices. She cuts her mark into her cell wall instead. Emotional beat: identity held like a blade.

chapters.title: The Governor's Fall
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The ship reaches the capital; the decrees are read into the colonial record; the Governor is recalled. Hale's authority evaporates overnight. Emotional beat: distant thunder of justice.

chapters.title: The Key in the Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Odile and Tam bribe and bluff their way to Hazel's cell; Elias arrives with lawful release papers signed by the new administration. Emotional beat: every kind of rescue at once—coin, cunning, and law.

chapters.title: Ashes and Sorts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel sifts the print shop ruins and salvages her father's first punch and a handful of surviving type. She decides to rebuild. Emotional beat: choosing to begin again from fragments.

chapters.title: A Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The shop reopens as 'Crane & Crane.' Hazel signs her first commission with her own name, witnessed by Elias, Marta, Tam, and Odile. Emotional beat: the quiet climax of self-claiming.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias resigns the census office to become the shop's proofreader and, haltingly, something more to Hazel. He hangs his old census ledger on the wall, crossed out. Emotional beat: a man finally home.

chapters.title: The Tide That Returns
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A year later: the first broadsheet of the new free press rolls off the rebuilt press, bearing the compass-lantern mark; Tam, now an apprentice, distributes it. Emotional beat: the found family's work outliving its dangers.

chapters.title: Compass and Lantern
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Closing chapter: Hazel teaches a new apprentice at the cutting bench, tells the truth of her history aloud for the first time, and lights the shop lantern against the evening fog. Emotional beat: belonging no longer earned, simply inhabited.
